headline: Machado is back in Venezuela. No election is set.
summary: María Corina Machado walked into a church in Lara state on Sunday, ten months after she fled the country to collect her Nobel Peace Prize. Her party says she tried to return seven times. US forces removed Maduro in January, but the acting president has stayed past her 90 days and called no election. Trump said he knew nothing about it.
cover_answer: She hid for 11 months, then was turned back seven times.
table_question: If you won a game but the ref said you lost, what would you do next?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: María Corina Machado went home to Venezuela today after almost a year away. She had to hide, then leave in secret by boat, because the people running her country wouldn't let her run against them. Today she walked into a church and the whole room hugged her, like a grandma at the airport. She's home now.
5-7.why: A homecoming is the whole story at this age. The hugs are the picture.
5-7.why_long: A seven-year-old reads a parent's face before the words and takes one feature for the whole event, so the script makes it a homecoming: the church, the hugs, the boat kept to one clause. Why she had to hide goes to the Try answer. Expect "is she safe now?" Trump said he hoped so. Nobody knows yet, and that is the honest answer.

8-12.script: In 2023 Machado won her side's primary with more than 90% of the vote. The government barred her, so an ally ran, and the AP says credible evidence shows he won 2-to-1. The election council named Maduro the winner anyway. Like a referee who also plays for one team.
8-12.why: Primary, ban, stand-in, a count nobody saw. The referee plays for one team.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out rules and whether the adults apply them, so the script hands them the chain: she won a primary, got barred, her stand-in won, the council said otherwise. The referee playing for one team is the mechanism. Expect "why didn't someone stop them?" The US did, in January. Then it picked the next president itself.

13-17.script: Is Venezuela freer than it was in December? Maduro is in a New York jail, and Machado walked into a church today to chants of "Freedom!" But the acting president the US backed was meant to serve 90 days, has stayed past them, and has called no election. Who turned her back?
13-17.why: Two true things: Maduro gone, no election set. Then the open question.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: Maduro is gone and nobody has been elected. The script asks who blocked the seven returns, which the AP leaves open: Venezuela's government denies it, US officials say they only advised her to wait. Expect "so was taking Maduro good or bad?" Say what you think, then show them the 90 days.

5-7.a: The bosses wouldn't let her run against them, so she hid. Today she made it home.

8-12.a: A council of ruling-party loyalists, the AP says. It never showed the tallies.
A New York jail. US forces took him in January. He says he's not guilty.

13-17.a: Unsettled. Activists blame Venezuela's government. The US says it advised.

13-17.q: Why does Trump say he knows nothing about it?
13-17.a: He told reporters so. Rubio, his secretary of state, credits US talks.
